A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PLADIS. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, quantitative benchmark results, human preference evaluations, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds GenEval evaluations, further framework comparisons, and extrapolation analyses.

M1.justification: PLADIS retains the dense/sparse cross-attention extrapolation, Algorithm 1, and default parameters. Equation 15 removes an extraneous argument from the dense-attention notation. The new output-based extrapolation variant is an experimental comparator, not a replacement procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds object-focused text-image evaluation on GenEval and a depth-conditioned ControlNet generation example (Tables 6 and 10; Figure 6). These extend coverage within image generation while retaining MS-COCO, Drawbench, HPD, and Pick-a-Pic.

E2.justification: v3 adds FreeU and ControlNet comparisons with and without PLADIS, an output-based extrapolation comparator, and identity/blur alternatives within the new in-model extrapolation experiment. Existing guidance and guidance-distilled comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce GenEval overall scores, Flux schnell/dev configurations, and in-model perturbation comparisons at lambda values 1.001 and 1.1. The original sampling budgets, guidance settings, and one-/four-step distilled-model protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands validation of the design. Figure 3 adds self-attention maps; Appendix G.4 compares in-model versus output-based extrapolation and sparse versus identity/blur perturbations. Appendix G.5 extends the sparse-only versus extrapolation analysis across five GenEval configurations. Earlier sensitivity and layer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and preference percentages without confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. v3 adds no seed or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are retained, but substantial new results appear. GenEval baseline/PLADIS scores are 0.671/0.713 for Flux schnell and 0.666/0.691 for Flux dev. Table 8 reports FID 29.48 for prediction-level versus 28.50 for in-model extrapolation. New qualitative findings cover ControlNet, FreeU, and perturbation failures; these are additions, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The retrieval-error bounds, noise-robustness statements, mathematical definitions, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Equation 15 receives a notation correction; Appendix G.4 adds conceptual interpretation rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about sparse-attention extrapolation, Hopfield-based justification, compatibility, and avoiding extra training or neural function evaluations. New experiments support those existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 refines the self-attention failure explanation through diagonal concentration, and Appendix G.4 argues that sparse attention preserves suitable Hopfield retrieval dynamics. v1's limitations section is removed, including the now-tested Flux limitation and the still-relevant qualification about untested video and language tasks.

D1.justification: v3 adds a PLADIS project/repository link in the abstract. Existing hardware, Entmax-library information, default parameters, and Appendix C implementation settings remain unchanged. Detailed implementation and evaluation instructions for the new extensions are limited.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for GenEval, Flux, FreeU, and ControlNet and positions PLADIS as compatible with the latter frameworks. The existing sparse-attention/Hopfield positioning and novelty claims remain intact.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites Sections 3.1–3.2, adds an extension paragraph and Appendix G.4–G.5, and removes the standalone limitations section. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 revises Figures 1 and 3, adds Figures 6 and 12 and Tables 6 and 10, and expands old Table 7 into Table 8. The unchanged user-study percentages are rearranged into stacked panels. These are localized display changes; the appendix galleries remain unchanged apart from numbering.

improvement.justification: The Flux evaluations address an explicitly acknowledged applicability gap, while Appendix G.4–G.5 provides useful evidence for choosing in-model extrapolation over alternatives. The project link also improves access information. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new experimental setups and removal of still-relevant limitations about untested non-image tasks.
